routes.description: Establish that religious faith is not needed to explain existence, experience, agency, morality, or meaning, and that grounding these domains in divine authority introduces epistemic and practical harms.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if naturalistic inquiry and human judgment can account for the motion's principal domains while projection, revelation, or sacred authority is shown to add no warranted explanation and to risk harmful consolation or coercion.

motionBridge.description: Connect the limits of religious explanation and the consequences of sacred authority to the motion-level claim that faith replaces reason with projection, authority, and harmful consolation.

centralBridges.description: Show that mystery, consciousness, transcendence, and cosmic origins do not warrant an inference to a personal or supervising deity.
Show that moral judgment and obligation can be articulated without divine command and that religious authority does not uniquely secure ethical conduct.
Show how divine mandates or institutional religious authority can magnify domination, violence, or resistance to secular moral constraints.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain why contingency, evolution, and human deliberation do not require an immaterial, divinely grounded source of freedom.
Account for awe, love, mortality, grief, and consolation without treating their human importance as evidence of supernatural truth.

routes.description: Establish that a transcendent source best grounds existence, consciousness, freedom, objective morality, and enduring meaning, while an evolving religious tradition can mediate those truths without requiring exhaustive knowledge of God.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if material explanation alone leaves central features of reality and human life insufficiently grounded, and if religious relationship, interpretation, community, and moral practice connect transcendence to freedom, obligation, and meaning.

motionBridge.description: Connect transcendent grounding and lived religious practice to the motion-level claim that faith reveals God, moral meaning, and human freedom.

centralBridges.description: Show why existence, consciousness, love, or recurrent awareness of transcendence can rationally indicate a reality beyond matter.
Show why universally binding moral truth requires a transcendent ground while still permitting interpretation and ethical reasoning.
Show how sacred relationship and religious community provide meaning, motivation, and consolation that are not reducible to factual error or psychological need.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain why genuine choice requires more than inherited biology and environment and how that additional basis relates to God.
Explain how a historically transmitted tradition can refine inherited defects while continuing to orient conduct toward justice and service.

sections.title: God, natural explanation, and standards of knowledge
sections.rationale: This issue tests the foundational inference from existence, consciousness, mystery, and recurring belief to God against projection accounts, scientific uncertainty, natural explanation, and the distinction between a first cause and a personal deity.

sections.title: Human freedom, material causation, and contingency
sections.rationale: The motion expressly places human freedom at issue, requiring comparison between the claim that agency needs an immaterial divine ground and the claim that evolutionary contingency and deliberation remain compatible with naturalism.

sections.title: Moral grounding, judgment, and religious authority
sections.rationale: This issue encompasses whether objective obligation depends on transcendence, whether shared human reasoning can ground ethical judgment, and whether scripture, interpretation, or secular institutions provide legitimate moral constraints.

sections.title: Meaning, transcendence, suffering, and consolation
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether experiences of sanctity, love, grief, mortality, and communal comfort disclose enduring sacred meaning or can be preserved through an honest naturalistic account without supernatural consolation.

sections.title: Religious practice, moral development, and social harm
sections.rationale: This issue weighs the burden-relevant causal claims about charity, service, evolving tradition, scriptural defects, proselytism, institutional abuse, tribal conflict, and the amplifying or disciplining effects of religious commitment.
